decisions.reason: As a recently launched carpet with its own page, it carries some visible commitment and sunk design/marketing cost, so management would be inclined to keep it unless overlap in the carpet range becomes too costly.

The hand-knotted wool-silk carpet fits the firm's craftsmanship and fine-material positioning, so despite any early uncertainty management would be inclined to justify the investment and continue with it.

This product is close to the existing offer and publicly introduced, which supports continuation, but as another low-pile decorative carpet it is somewhat more exposed to rationalization if the range proves crowded.
The corner bench builds directly on the established furniture business and likely serves residential and project interiors, making it easier for management to defend continued support.

Management would tend to persist with this recently introduced carpet because resources and reputation have already been committed, though carpets are less central than core furniture lines and easier to trim if needed.

A swivel shell chair line with several models implies broader investment and stronger public commitment, and it fits workplace and flexible interior concepts, so escalation of commitment strongly favors keeping it.
